# authwise_application_secret (Resource)

An application's secret (its OAuth `client_secret`), for authenticating it to the token endpoint. kit creates it and returns it once, so the secret is kept in state: treat the state as sensitive.

Formerly `authwise_client_secret` (kit#968): a `moved` block from `authwise_client_secret` carries the state across, `secret` included.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Application-scoped: a secret for a machine application. kit creates it and returns it
# once; Terraform keeps it in state and hands it on from there.
resource "authwise_application" "ci" {
  display_name = "CI"
  grant_types  = ["client_credentials"]
}

resource "authwise_application_secret" "ci" {
  application_id = authwise_application.ci.application_id
  expires_at     = "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"

  # kit has no rotate verb: change a keeper to create a successor. With
  # create_before_destroy the new secret exists before the old one goes.
  keepers = {
    rotation = "2026-09"
  }

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

# the OAuth client_secret
output "ci_client_secret" {
  value     = authwise_application_secret.ci.secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `application_id` (String) Parent identifier `application_id`; overrides the provider default, and reads back from the name. Changing a configured one replaces the resource.
- `expires_at` (String) `expires_at` as an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `issuer_id` (String) Parent identifier `issuer_id`; overrides the provider default, and reads back from the name. Changing a configured one replaces the resource.
- `keepers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values that replace the resource when any of them changes, never sent to the API. Change one to rotate: with `create_before_destroy`, the successor is created before this one is deleted.
- `tenant_id` (String) Parent identifier `tenant_id`; overrides the provider default, and reads back from the name. Changing a configured one replaces the resource.

### Read-Only

- `application_secret_id` (String) Server-assigned resource id — the last segment of `name`, and what other resources' `*_id` attributes take.
- `hash_enabled` (Boolean)
- `name` (String) Full resource name; serves as the Terraform ID.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) Returned once, by `CreateApplicationSecret`, and kept in state: no read returns it, so a resource brought in with `terraform import` has none. Replace the resource (see `keepers`) to get a new one.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by full resource name. The secret cannot be recovered: an imported
# application secret has no `secret` until a keepers change creates a new one.
terraform import authwise_application_secret.example tenants/t-01/issuers/i-01/applications/c-01/application-secrets/cs-01
```
